author: Autodesk
description: This graph demonstrates the use of the RBD solver as pre-roll.
documentation:
## Scatter and Settle (instant)

### What it does
This graph uses the RBD system enable a "pre-rolled" starting point for a simulation.  This allows for as many frames as desired while still retaining the ability to simulate.

### Inputs and outputs
This graph is self-contained, the "dice" and floor collider shapes are generated internally (inside the ***generate_geometry*** compound) and the output is both simulated geometry and rendered instances.

### How it works
A set of points are generated in a vertical stack, dice primitives (platonic solids) are instanced onto those points, the starting positions is controlled by a seed.  

The setting *preroll_frames* on the ***rigid_body_solver_settings*** compound instructs the solver to simulate up until that frame.  The *start_frame* setting on ***rigid_body_solver_settings*** must match the current frame on the Maya timeline for this system to perform as preroll.

metadata.description: This graph demonstrates the use of the RBD solver as pre-roll.

_notes.text:
It is **very important** that the timeline is the same as the *start_frame* set on this compound.

To instantly scatter and settle, change the ***preroll_frames*** setting.

This allows playing the simulation to a certain point, using that as a preroll to any following simulation.
The simulation calculates based on the lighter collision geo, but renders the higher-re and heavier render geo.

_backdrops.title: Makes the "tray" the dice fall onto

_notes.text:
This compound creates platonic solids and one non platonic solid.  These are custom builds  so please feel free to dive in and investigate.

The compound outputs both very simple geo (*sim_geo*) for simulation as well as higher-res geo (*render_geo*) for rendering.
This compound gets the geo ready for simulation. Changing the seed will change the shape of the final settled output.
This compound sets up your "dice bag" - how many dice, whether they're sequential (default) or random.

Array in order:

d20
d12
d6
d8
d4
d10

_backdrops.title: 4 points on the corners of the unit cube
4 points on the corners of the unit cube

_notes.text:
Rather than baking the instances to a mesh, this compound extracts both the render and collision geos from the instance object.

This is done for speed and is only a viable option when the instance count is low.  This graph has 6 unique instances.
